text:
alex (ceo): quick follow-up from todays all-hands Q&A. key asks: clearer messaging vs competitors, concrete SLO guidance for product teams, and a short playbook for sales. dropping a short thread to capture decisions.

mira (vp-product): thanks. PMs want a single source of truth: one exec-friendly line, one technical blurb, and a decision tree for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. can leadership confirm?

alex (ceo): confirmed. exec line: "Redwood: production-first inference that gives developers a simple API plus predictable performance and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." technical blurb: "single high-throughput runtime, workload-aware batching & prefix caching, and policy-based smart routing for cost/latency tradeoffs."

omar (dir-platform): for the SLOs: engineering asked for thresholds to drive prioritization. suggest we publish a tiny matrix (Hosted: p50 < 100ms, Dedicated: p50 < 60ms, Private: negotiated) plus reliability bands. ok to make that guidance?

alex (ceo): yes — publish guidance, not hard limits. use those numbers to decide when kernel/runtime work must jump the queue for Dedicated deals.

jamie (sales-eng): sales needs a short objection-handling line: when customers compare us to vendors that only provide model access or only on-prem boxes. what's the recommended phrasing?

alex (ceo): use contrast language: "Unlike providers that focus only on model access or only on on-prem hardware, Redwood unifies developer velocity with production economics and deployment flexibility." keep it non-branded but clear.

sasha (customer-success): also capture proof points: a mini case study on hosted->dedicated migration and a latency chart for a representative workload. sales asks for these in the playbook.

mira (vp-product): noted. we'll include a 1-paragraph migration story, a latency CDF, and a checklist for Private installs.

ops-bot: created task T-5987 in #product-ops: "Publish exec line, technical blurb, SLO guidance, and sales playbook (incl. proofs)" assigned to @mira and @jamie, due in 3 business days.

alex (ceo): final note on prioritization: teams should prioritize work that unlocks committed ARR first. non-revenue-blocking UX improvements can be scheduled after that. if you think your project is a blocker, ping me or drop the rationale in #product-roadmap.

omar (dir-platform): i'll prepare the SLO draft and a short runbook for engineering tradeoffs.

mira (vp-product): i'll draft copy and the playbook, post in #product-ops for review. thanks all — will link the docs here when ready. :thumbsup:
